verses.text: In the first month the whole community of Israel arrived in the desert of Zin, and they stayed at Kadesh. There Miriam died and was buried.
There was no water for the community, so the people gathered against Moses and Aaron.
They argued with Moses and said, "We wish we had died when our brothers died before the LORD!
Why did you bring the LORD's people into this desert? So that we and our animals would die here?
Why did you make us leave Egypt and bring us to this terrible place? There is no grain, no figs, no grapevines, and no pomegranates here. There is not even water to drink!"
Moses and Aaron left the crowd and went to the door of the Tent of Meeting. They bowed down with their faces to the ground, and the glory of the LORD appeared to them.
The LORD said to Moses,

"Take the walking stick, and you and your brother Aaron gather the community together. While they watch, speak to that rock, and it will pour out its water. In this way you will bring water out of the rock for the community and their animals to drink."
So Moses took the stick from its place before the LORD, as the LORD had commanded him.
Moses and Aaron gathered the people in front of the rock, and Moses said to them, "Listen, you rebels! Must we bring water out of this rock for you?"
Then Moses raised his hand and hit the rock twice with his stick. Water poured out, plenty of it, and the community and their animals drank.
But the LORD said to Moses and Aaron, "Because you did not trust me enough to show my holiness in front of the people of Israel, you will not lead this community into the land I am giving them."
This was the water of Meribah, which means arguing, because there the people of Israel argued with the LORD, and he showed them that he is holy.
From Kadesh, Moses sent messengers to the king of Edom. They said, "This is what your brother Israel says: You know about all the hardships we have been through.
Our ancestors went down to Egypt, and we lived there for many years. The Egyptians treated us and our ancestors cruelly.
But when we cried out to the LORD, he heard us and sent an angel and brought us out of Egypt. Now we are here at Kadesh, a town on the edge of your land.

Please let us pass through your country. We will not go through your fields or vineyards, or drink water from any well. We will stay on the King's Highway and not turn to the right or the left until we have passed through your land."
But Edom answered, "You may not pass through here. If you try, we will come out and attack you with our swords."
The people of Israel replied, "We will stay on the main road. If we or our animals drink any of your water, we will pay for it. We only want to pass through on foot, nothing else."
But Edom answered again, "You may not pass through." Then Edom came out against them with a large and powerful army.
Since Edom refused to let Israel pass through their land, Israel turned away from them.
The whole community of Israel set out from Kadesh and came to Mount Hor.
At Mount Hor, near the border of Edom, the LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
"Aaron is going to die and join his people who have died. He will not enter the land I am giving to the people of Israel, because both of you rebelled against my command at the water of Meribah.
Take Aaron and his son Eleazar up Mount Hor.
Take off Aaron's priestly clothes and put them on his son Eleazar. Aaron will die there and join his people."
Moses did what the LORD commanded. They went up Mount Hor while the whole community watched.
Moses took off Aaron's clothes and put them on his son Eleazar. And Aaron died there on top of the mountain. Then Moses and Eleazar came down from the mountain.
When the whole community learned that Aaron had died, all the people of Israel mourned for him for thirty days.
